minutes.headline: Water commissioners denied a leak abatement and set a November 17 special meeting to fill the vacant seat.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners denied a bill abatement for a leak past the meter, extended a new hire's probation, and scheduled a special meeting to fill the seat vacated by a resigning commissioner. They also discussed the cell tower license, tank inspection and cleaning, the Hickory Hills well and contingency planning, and authorized signing the audit agreement.

public_comment.topic: A resident asked about the cost of the audit agreement and then urged a contingency plan, possibly with escrowed funds, for the Hickory Hills well and manganese in case of a supply emergency.
Same resident noted a proposed large warehouse on Shirley Road that might need water service.

votes.motion: Deny the request for abatement of the bill for the pool house leak on Northfield Road.
Hold a special meeting on November 17 to fill the vacant commissioner seat.
Authorize the superintendent and a commissioner to sign the auditor agreement for the next audit.

budget_items.what_was_said: A new owner asked for a reduction for a leak in a pool house line after the meter; the board noted it does not abate usage after the meter and still bears production costs.
Discussion that carrier rent from the tank pays for tank maintenance and a separate tower would cost the district rent; the 1996 betterment charge was cited as the alternative.
Quotes were obtained for tank inspection and cleaning; the superintendent prefers cleaning in house and paying from the maintenance budget.
A resident asked the audit cost; the fee was said to be the same as in past years and capped, with the typical price recalled.
Treatment is cost prohibitive; grant or state revolving fund money was suggested.

transfers.description: Asked whether a transfer is needed for tank inspection and cleaning; answered that it is usually in the maintenance budget.

decisions.decision: Board agreed to extend the new hire's probation period another six months.
Board will move toward an RFP for the cell tower license, pending the attorney's final view.
Superintendent to proceed with tank inspection and cleaning from the maintenance budget.
Next meeting set for September 22 at 4 pm; interested candidates encouraged to introduce themselves.

what_happened.line: Water commissioners voted to deny a bill abatement for a leak in a pool house line on Northfield Road, past the meter.
The board voted to hold a special meeting on November 17 to fill the commissioner seat left vacant by a resignation.
Commissioners agreed to extend a new hire's probation by another six months.
The board will move toward an RFP for the cell tower license, pending the attorney's final view.
The superintendent will proceed with tank inspection and cleaning, paid from the maintenance budget, and a vote authorized signing the audit agreement.

why_it_matters: Water customers are billed for usage through the meter, and the board's reasoning for the denial was that the district still bears production costs, so a leak after the meter stays on the customer's bill.
Cell tower rent from the tank helps pay for tank maintenance, so how the license is rebid bears on what the district must raise from water rates.

A resident raised the Hickory Hills well and manganese, where treatment was described as cost prohibitive and grant or state revolving fund money was suggested, so supply planning could later mean a funding request.
